content:
Who decided that Wang Fuk Court residents cannot return?

Many owners raised the issue during the Q&A session. At least five questioners at the meeting questioned Hop On, asking which department decided residents cannot return to Wang Fuk Court and what legal basis there was for the cordoning-off. Hop On initially did not give a direct answer for the first four times, merely saying that Wang Fuk Court has not yet been unsealed and that it is beyond the manager's authority to arrange, and advised owners to contact a one-household-one-social-worker if needed, which at one point triggered an outcry among owners in several venues.

Hop On does not know on what legal basis the authorities cordoned off the area

Solicitor Leung Ping-chiu finally responded by saying that Hop On did not know on what legal basis the authorities carried out the cordoning-off, but it was not appropriate to explain on their behalf for fear of misrepresenting the government's considerations. As for the survey reports of the other seven buildings at Wang Fuk Court, which also drew much attention, Hop On said that the typhoon and rainy seasons are approaching, and the findings may be released after the authorities complete the survey; it also said that after taking legal advice, Hop On was of the view that such requests fall beyond its duties as manager.

Owners concerned government using donations to acquire titles, not rebuilding could save compensation for China Taiping?

The government previously said it would not rebuild on the original site. At the meeting, many owners were concerned whether this meant that the HK$2 billion "fire insurance" payout, calculated on the cost of restoring the building's structure, would not be honoured. "Is it the case that by using donations to take back the titles and not rebuilding, the government can save China Taiping the compensation?" Ms Liu, representative of China Taiping Insurance (Hong Kong), said that once policy liability is established, the company will pay out in accordance with the policy terms regardless of whether repairs or rebuilding will take place, and that any acquisition would not affect policy liability or the calculation of amounts. But Liu also said the specifics of the policy and legal liability can only be further assessed after the independent committee and relevant government departments complete their investigations and release their findings.

Revealed that repairing Wang Chi House would cost HK$30 million

Hop On also reported on the situation of Wang Chi House, which was unaffected by the disaster. Hop On had previously said that if repairs were needed, the project would cost at least HK$30 million and take at least nine months, involving re-tiling the external walls and restoring the electricity supply, among other works; today it updated the total to about HK$32 million, with a construction period of three to nine months. Solicitor Leung Ping-chiu, invited by Hop On to attend the meeting, said Wang Chi House is part of the entire estate under the Deed of Mutual Covenant, and separating it out would require extensive DMC amendments with the consent of all owners — a complicated and costly process.

Some owners noted that Hop On had used the excuse that contacting owners took time and therefore failed to convene an owners' meeting within the statutory deadline, yet had successfully issued funding cheques on behalf of the Urban Renewal Authority earlier this year. They questioned: "I'd like to ask what's so difficult — you can't find us owners to hold a meeting?" Leung Wai-kong, Hop On's property services chief who chaired the meeting, did not give a direct answer, saying it was a venue issue and that it was difficult to find a venue that could accommodate a thousand residents; only when the Home Affairs Department provided a venue could the meeting be held. Some owners criticised the explanation as unreasonable: "In Hong Kong you put on all those grand economic events, easily staging a show for tens of thousands in one venue, and you're telling me there's not one place that can accommodate our 2,000 people? That's really hard to accept. I hope you won't use this as an excuse again."
